validity.recommendation: Drop 'Urengoy gas field' from FuelSource; keep only the Yamal-Peninsula source (Bovanenkovskoye), which is what every primary source found for this specific pipeline actually names. Gazprom's own dedicated design page for this line (proektirovanie.gazprom.ru) states it carries gas 'с полуострова Ямал' (from the Yamal Peninsula) and explicitly distinguishes this corridor from the separate, historically Urengoy/North-Tyumen-fed 'СРТО — Торжок' trunk that also runs through the same technical corridor -- i.e. Urengoy gas has a DIFFERENT dedicated pipeline (SRTO-Torzhok) sharing the right-of-way, which is the likely source of the sheet's conflation. World Pipelines independently ties the exact 2018-12-06 commissioning to the Bovanenkovskoye field's third production facility, with zero mention of Urengoy. No source checked (Gazprom's own site, Gazprom Proektirovanie, World Pipelines, Pravda Severa) names Urengoy gas as entering this specific line. Recommend a human confirm before dropping, in case a small blended volume of Urengoy-originated gas legitimately enters at the Ukhta hub (the two field-sourced supplies are already commingled in the Unified Gas Supply System by the time they reach Ukhta), but as a discrete named FuelSource it is unsupported.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Status review in annual-update mode. Verdict: CONFIRM operating. Ukhta-Torzhok-2 is a domestic Northwestern-Russia gas-distribution trunk moving Yamal-Peninsula gas from Ukhta to the Gryazovets hub, feeding the Unified Gas Supply System's northern corridor for onward domestic distribution and further trunks -- it is not itself an export pipeline exposed to the 2022 Nord Stream sabotage, EU sanctions, or Baltic-connection disruptions that justify re-examining several sibling rows in this batch. Pravda Severa (2022-04-07, the newest independently-dated evidence found for this row) quotes Gazprom Transgaz Ukhta's own general director naming it among the company's currently-realized major projects at his annual press conference, seven weeks before the invasion-era sanctions took effect -- i.e. still in active service in early 2022, with no operational disruption specific to this domestic line plausible or evidenced since. World Pipelines (2018-12-06) independently confirms original commissioning/connection to the UGSS. No source found (Gazprom, Gazprom Proektirovanie, World Pipelines, Pravda Severa, or the harvested wiki_citations pool) indicates decommissioning, mothballing, damage, or any other status change for this specific line at any point. Recommend keeping Status=operating unchanged.
